note: Single coherence record tying SDK source behavior to LLVM type layouts and decoder assumptions for the classifier (packet/parse/checksum/scalar) programs and the fixed 32-byte event record. Every numeric claim is machine-checked by tests/elf/test_layouts.py (classifier rows) or tests/elf/test_event_struct.py (event rows) against genuine build artifacts; prose claims name their owning suite. Map BTF and map decoding belong to the map contract suite and are referenced, not duplicated, here.

source_behavior.guard_idiom: Every packet load is dominated by a length guard that fails closed to XDP_DROP. Two forms: start-based packet_short(ctx, need) checks need bytes from the packet start; address-based addr_short(addr, ctx, size) checks size bytes at one computed address. The guarded address and the loaded address are one shared computation; packet_base runs exactly once per program.
source_behavior.byte_orders: Packet loads assemble little-endian from single bytes at any alignment. Header fields travel big-endian: the parse accessors swap after the little-endian load and callers compare against ordinary protocol numbers. The independent oracles decode with int.from_bytes and never mirror the shift-or assembly.
source_behavior.checksum: Callers accumulate network-order words into a 32-bit sum with explicit unrolled adds, then fold carries in two stages and complement. The independent oracle folds with a carry loop and complements by subtraction.
source_behavior.no_packed_struct_cast: No classifier casts packet bytes to a struct. All packet-rooted loads are 8-bit at guarded offsets; multi-byte values are assembled from bytes. The layout suite scans every classifier's adapted IR and fails on any wider packet-rooted load.
source_behavior.integers: Fixed-width two's-complement integers with native wrap. Mojo Int is 64-bit signed. Scalar aliases implemented over one-lane SIMD keep these widths and are not rejected for their representation.

frontend.note: The Mojo frontend emits host-target IR; the adapter retargets it before the BPF backend. SDK value-type sizes are identical under both data layouts.

kernel.note: Kernel-visible layout after adaptation. Pointers and 64-bit integers are 8 bytes, little-endian, matching the host legs for every SDK value type.

classifier_loads.note: In classifier IR, every load rooted at the packet reinterpretation is 8 bits and every load rooted at the context argument is 32 bits at offset 0 (data) or 4 (data_end). The data_meta word (offset 8) has its XdpCtx slot but its load is eliminated when unused. The address chain's plus-one check shares the syntactic shape of a start-based guard with need 1; the suite expects that extra 1 for the two address shapes and proves the chain shape separately.

context_words.note: Kernel xdp_md leading words. Offsets 0/4 are read by every classifier; offset 8 is the XdpCtx data_meta slot.

actions.note: XDP action codes per the kernel UAPI. The guard trip returns drop; the entry point returns a 32-bit action.

map_slots.note: One-entry array vocabulary owned by the map SDK and pinned structurally by the map contract suite, plus the two-entry array the combined packet workload counts into (pinned by the combined structure suite); widths repeated here for the decoder row only.

decoder_assumptions.entry_signature: i32 @xdp_entry(ptr): the test-run decoder reads a 32-bit return as the XDP action. Checked on every classifier.
decoder_assumptions.license_bytes: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception plus NUL in the license section. Checked on a classifier object.
decoder_assumptions.classifier_btf: Absent by design: classifiers carry no maps, hence no BTF. Checked on a classifier object. Map BTF is owned by the map contract suite.
decoder_assumptions.test_run: Actions observed through the revision-2 test-run harness with crafted frames; staged hashes re-verified in-guest. Owned by the kernel suites.
decoder_assumptions.map_decoding: Fixed key/value widths with exact entry counts; per-CPU totals decoded with the possible-CPU count and value padding. Owned by the kernel map suites.
decoder_assumptions.oracle_orders: Independent oracles decode fields with int.from_bytes (big-endian for header fields, little-endian for context words) and fold checksums with a carry loop. Owned by the differential and kernel suites.
